audience.text: Java developers building server-side or desktop applications that require PDF document generation, manipulation, and extraction without third-party runtime dependencies.

capabilities.text: Build pages from scratch using Document, Page, and Paragraphs to add text, tables, and form elements.
capabilities.title: Create and modify PDF documents

capabilities.text: Use TextAbsorber to extract plain text and iterate XImage resources to save images to files.
capabilities.title: Extract text and images

capabilities.text: Access and modify form fields including TextBoxField and RadioButtonOptionField through the Form facade.
capabilities.title: Work with AcroForm fields

capabilities.text: Set and read annotation properties such as border color, background color, and border style.
capabilities.title: Configure annotations and widget characteristics

capabilities.text: Apply resource optimization, encrypt with AES/RC4, and sign with PKCS#7 via dedicated APIs.
capabilities.title: Optimize and secure documents

capabilities.text: Convert documents to PDF/A and validate against PDF/A-1 through PDF/A-4 requirements.
capabilities.title: Convert and validate PDF standards

limitations.text: No OCR support for recognizing text in scanned images; a dedicated OCR library is required.
Concurrency is not supported for a single Document instance; separate instances are required for parallel processing.
Text replacement with non-Latin scripts may differ from reference renderers due to limited bidirectional reordering and shaping.
Resource optimization has limited advanced strategies; image downsampling and font merging across resources are constrained.
Tagged PDF structure trees are readable and constructible but not fully covered for well-formedness.
PDF/X validation and conversion lack dedicated test coverage despite API support.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic creation and modification of PDF documents including text, tables, forms, annotations, and images using a consistent Java API.
Supports extraction of text and images from existing PDFs for indexing, analysis, or repurposing content.
Provides form field population and interaction capabilities for AcroForm and RadioButtonOptionField elements.
Offers document optimization, security (encryption/signing), and conversion to PDF/A or HTML without external libraries.

product_summary.text: Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java is a free, open-source, pure-Java library for creating, reading, and modifying PDF documents, targeting ISO 32000-1:2008 compliance.

uncertainties: The exact scope of 'partial' tagged PDF support beyond what is stated in the inherited README is unclear.
Whether 'basic stream recompression' in resource optimization covers all common compression algorithms is not specified.
The behavior of XFA form conversion to AcroForm when dynamic layout features are present is not detailed beyond flattening.
The thread-safety boundary for Document instances and related objects is not explicitly defined beyond the Document itself.
